A1.justification: Both complete, readable 11-page PDFs describe the same VideoFusion/M3SVD study. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of equations, figures and tables. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original fusion experiments on M3SVD and HDO, temporal-consistency analyses, object-tracking examples, efficiency measurements and ablations in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 5, including quantitative comparisons in Tables 2–5 and qualitative evidence in Figures 5–10.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same VideoFusion architecture, CmDRM, CMGF, BiCAM, modality-unmixing components and loss functions. No algorithm, objective or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same M3SVD and HDO coverage, normal and degraded fusion scenarios, and M3SVD object-tracking evaluation. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical, including the nine fusion baselines in Tables 2–3 and the MDIVDNet and DSTNet restoration methods in Section 5.1 and Table 4.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 retain training on 200 M3SVD videos for 20 epochs, evaluation on 20 videos from each dataset, and identical degradations, model configurations and metrics.

E4.justification: The temporal-consistency analyses in Figures 6–7, tracking case study in Figure 8, and module/loss ablations in Table 5 and Figures 9–10 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting is identical. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports VideoFusion's degraded-M3SVD MI as 4.027 and SSIM as 0.635 in both versions; Tables 3–5 and the result figures also match.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(13), their mathematical definitions, and the temporal-variation assumptions surrounding Equation (11) are identical. No derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about the 220-video M3SVD dataset, joint spatial-temporal fusion, degradation handling and improved temporal consistency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of temporal flickering, complementary information and ablation outcomes are unchanged, including the explanation that removing CMGF can raise SF/SD while introducing artifacts. No new limitations or applicability qualifications appear.

D1.justification: Data acquisition and registration procedures, degradation generation, hyperparameters, optimizer schedule and hardware disclosures in Sections 4–5.1 are identical. No code or dataset access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, research positioning throughout the paper and all 58 numbered references are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 corrects 'Mutli-modal' to 'Multi-modal' in the title and updates the first-page arXiv version/date stamp. The remaining prose, terminology and section structure are identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–5 retain identical content, captions, formatting and placement. Pages 2–11 render identically; the first-page differences are confined to title and version/date text.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes a title typo and updates the arXiv stamp, providing cosmetic polish. The scientific exposition, methods, evidence, interpretations and reproducibility information remain identical, so overall paper quality does not meaningfully change.
